These Appeals, Coming On For Admission, This
Day, G Basavaraja, J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Both the appeals are arising out of judgment and award dated 13th July, 2017 passed in MVC No.2597 of 2015 by the X Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi (for short, hereinafter referred to as the "Tribunal").

entities.text: X Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in these appeals are referred to as per their status and rank before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8918-DB

On November 9, 2015, Krishna Subhash Gowda, who was the rider of the motorcycle with registration No. KA-22/EM- 8770, was traveling on Vadagaon-Yallur road at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.
At approximately 5:30 pm, as he approached the Government Marathi School, he collided with the rear portion of the petitioner's motorcycle, registered as KA-22/ES-4975.

This collision resulted in the petitioner falling along with his Sri. Shivaji S/O Kallappa Navagekar vs Smt. Yallawwa W/O Subhashchandra ... on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161670834/
3 motorcycle and sustaining grievous injuries.
4. At the time of the accident, the petitioner was 32 years old and engaged in centering work,
earning a monthly income of Rs.20,000/-.

entities.text: Sri. Shivaji S/O Kallappa Navagekar vs Smt. Yallawwa W/O Subhashchandra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he suffered a permanent residual physical disability, leading to the loss of his earning capacity.
Additionally, he incurred significant expenses for medical treatment and other purposes.
These circumstances form the basis for the petitioner's claim for compensation.
5. Pursuant to the issuance of notice, respondent No.2 appeared through their counsel and filed a written statement.
Respondent No.1 was declared exparte.

In the substance of the NC:
2023:KHC-D:8918-DB written statement provided by respondent No.2, it is argued that the rider of the offending motorcycle with registration No. KA-22/ES-4975 did not possess a valid and effective driving license for that class of vehicle on the date of the accident.
The police have also charged the said rider under Section 3 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Consequently, respondent No.2, the Insurance Company, cannot be held liable to indemnify respondent No. 1.
6.
Furthermore, it is contended that the accident occurred due to the petitioner's own rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle.
Therefore, the owner and insurer of the motorcycle ridden by the petitioner should be considered necessary parties in the proceedings.
In their absence, it is argued that, the petitioner's claim is not maintainable.
The respondent No. 2 has also denied the other averments made in the claim petition and seeks the dismissal of the petition.

7. Based on the rival pleadings, the Tribunal has formulated following issues for its consideration:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in a RTA that occurred on NC: 2023:KHC-D:8918-DB 09.11.2015 at about 17.31 hours on Vadagaon-Yallur Road, near Govt. Marathi School due to rash and negligent riding of Hero Honda Splendor Motorcycle bearing Reg No.KA-22/ES-4965 by its rider?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, or what amount and from whom?

3. To what award?
8.
To substantiate his case, the petitioner examined two witnesses as PWs1 and 2 marked twelve documents as Exhibits P1 and P12.
Respondent No.2-Insurance Company adduced evidence of RW1 and produced exhibits R1 to R9.

In light of the above findings, the Tribunal partially allowed the petition and awarded compensation of Rs.1,79,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim Sri. Shivaji S/O Kallappa Navagekar vs Smt. Yallawwa W/O Subhashchandra ...

on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161670834/
4 petition until full realisation.

The insurance company, aggrieved by this judgment and award, NC:
2023:KHC-D:8918-DB filed Miscellaneous First Appeal No.103367 of 2017, challenging the liability.
Simultaneously, the claimant also filed Miscellaneous First Appeal No.102890 of 2017, seeking an enhancement in compensation.

10. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the Tribunal has not properly appreciated and considered the oral and documentary evidence on record produced by the parties in proper perspective.
The Tribunal has erred in not considering the objections of the Insurance Company.

Further, he submits that the Tribunal has not considered the charge sheet submitted by the Investigating Officer under Sections 3 and 5 of the Motor Vehicles Act against the rider and also the owner of the motorcycle.
The Tribunal has also failed to appreciate the fact the respondent No.1 has violated policy conditions.
On all these grounds sought to allow the appeal.

11. Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that the Tribunal has rightly held that the accident occurred on the rash and negligent act on the part of the offending motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-22/ES-4975.
He further submits that the Tribunal has not awarded just and proper compensation in accordance with law and facts and hence sought for enhancement of compensation.

12. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, the following points arise for our consideration in these appeals:
(1) Whether the Insurance Company has made out a ground for interference with impugned judgment and award as to its liability is concerned?
(2) Whether the appellant-claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?

(3)
What order or award?
14. We have carefully examined the material on record.
Based on the complaint filed by Shivaji Kallappa Navagekar, the Belgaum South Police registered the case under Crime No. 184 of 2015 against the rider of the new Hero Honda Splendor.
The NC: 2023:KHC-D:8918-DB charges were for offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of the Indian Penal Code, as well as Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Subsequently, the police conducted various investigations, including a spot panchnama, preparation of a rough sketch, and a seizure panchnama of the vehicles involved in the accident.
They also obtained a report from a Motor Vehicles Inspector and a wound certificate.

Additionally, the police recorded statements from witnesses and filed a charge sheet against the rider of the Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle, accused No.1-Krishna Subashchandra Goudar, for Sri. Shivaji S/O Kallappa Navagekar vs Smt. Yallawwa W/O Subhashchandra ... on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161670834/
5 offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of the Indian Penal Code, read with Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Accused No.2-Yellavva Subhashchandra Goudar, was also charge sheeted for offences under Sections 5 and 180 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Considering the evidence on record, the Tribunal, at paragraph 15 of the judgment, has observed as under:
"15.

Regarding Liability:
A contention is raised by the respondent No.2 that, at the time of occurrence of this accident, the driver of the insured motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA.22/ES4975 did not have a valid and effective driving licence and the insured respondent No.1 knowing full well this fact had entrusted his said vehicle to him to drive on the public road and as - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8918-DB such the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the insured respondent No.1 for breach of policy conditions.
The RW.1 who happens to be an official witness of the respondent NO.2 has reiterated this above facts in his evidence.
It is to not that, the burden to prove that the rider of the insured vehicle did not have a valid and effective driving licence at the time of occurrence of this accident, is on the insurer
But, the insurer has not made any efforts to summon the rider and no any records from Regional Transport Authority was produced to substantiate its above contention.
It is true that the rider of insured vehicle has been charge sheeted under section 3 r/w 181 of M.V. Act in addition to section 279 and 338 ofIPC by the jurisdictional police.
Whether the police charge sheet could be relied upon to hold that the rider had no driving licence?, is a point to be taken into consideration.

It is to note that, our own Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Ratna and Another reported in 2017 ACJ 646 has held that, in theabsence of any evidence on record to show that the rider of the insured motorcycle had no driving licence as on the date of the accident, the charge sheet filed by the police alone cannot be made basis to hold that the said driver had no driving licence.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Ratna and Another reported in 2017 ACJ 646
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This decision has been rendered relying upon a decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Rukmini Vs. New India Assurance Company Ltd., and others reported in 1999 ACJ 171 (SC), by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

entities.text: Rukmini Vs. New India Assurance Company Ltd., and others reported in 1999 ACJ 171 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In viewof this decision, I am of the considered opinion that the insured who has failed to examine the rider of the offending motorcycle and who has failed to produce the record from the Regional - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8918-DB Transport Authority, cannot rely upon the police charge sheet to contend that the motorcyclist had no driving licence at the time of occurrence of this accident.
Consequently, I hold that the respondent No.2 has failed to prove that the rider of the insured motorcycle had no valid and effective driving Sri.

entities.text: Shivaji S/O Kallappa Navagekar vs Smt. Yallawwa
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6 licence as on the date of the accident.

In the result, the respondent No.1 being the registered owner/insured and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.NO.KA.22/ES 4975 are jointly and severally liable to pay aforesaid award amount together with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realisation of the entire award amount to the petitioner.

However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the aforesaid award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order by way of indemnifying the insured respondent No.1 under the contract of insurance policy.
With these observation, I shall conclude my discussion by answering the Issue No.2 framed herein above partly in the affirmative in favour of the petitioner.

"
15. That on re-appreciation/re-consideration and re- evaluation of the record, we do not find any legal infirmities/illegalities in the finding given by the Tribunal regarding the liability of Insurance Company.
Hence, we answer the point No.1 in the negative.

With regard to quantum of compensation is concerned, the petitioner has produced Exhibit P7-wound certificate issued by Vijaya Ortho and Trauma Centre, Belagavi, which reveals that the petitioner has suffered the following injuries:

entities.text: Vijaya Ortho and Trauma Centre, Belagavi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Exhibit P10 is the disability certificate; Exhibit P11 is the X-ray film and Exhibit P10 is x-ray report.

The evidence of PWs1 and 2 and Exhibits P7 to P12 reveals that soon after the accident, the injured was taken to Vijaya Ortho and Trauma Centre, Belagavi for treatment and he was inpatient there from 09th to 12th November, 2015.

entities.text: Vijaya Ortho and Trauma Centre, Belagavi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The Doctor has given final diagnosis as follows:
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8918-DB "a.

There is malunion of the above fractures; d. He cannot do abduction and adduction in the right fore foot joint;
e.
There is limitation of motion in the right floot with severe pain."
16. The Tribunal assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs. 7,000/- per month, which does not align with the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

According to the guidelines, for accidents occurring in the year 2015, the notional income should be Rs.
8,000/- per month, and therefore, this higher figure is considered.
Furthermore, the Tribunal evaluated the petitioner's total disability at 5%, which appears to be on the lower side given the nature of injuries and the evidence.
It is reasonable to adjust the disability percentage to 8% for the entire body.
The Tribunal correctly applied a multiplier of 17.
Consequently, the loss of future earnings is calculated at Rs.1,30,500/- (Rs.8,000/- x 12 x 17 x 8%).

Considering the nature of injuries, pain and suffering, it is just and proper to award the compensation as follows:
- 14 -  NC: 2023:KHC-D:8918-DB  Amount Sl.No. Head  (in Rs.)
1. Pain and suffering 30,000 2. Loss of earning during laid up 32,000  period 3. Loss of future income 1,30,500 4. Loss of amenities 25,000 5.
Medical and other incidental 25,000  expenses

In the result, we pass the following:
 ORDER 1.
Miscellaneous First Appeal No.103367 of 2017 filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed;

3. Judgment and award dated 13th July, 2017 passed in MVC No.2597 of 2015 is modified by enhancing the compensation to Rs.2,42,500/- as against Rs.1,79,400/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
The same shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
4. Amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the Tribunal for onward disbursal to the claimant;
